artifacts.summary: Confirms the // 1 default bug in skill_read_artifact_number() (skill-base.sh) masks the legacy fallback; identifies skill-reviser/SKILL.md's existing max-prefix reconciliation scan as directly reusable prior art; finds no core creation path currently writes pre-supplied non-empty artifacts[] (so round-resolution is the necessary fix, creation-time write is optional); and finds orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh carries zero next_artifact_number logic, recommending the three declared territory edges against it be dropped.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's agent-system/extensions/core, skill-base.sh's skill_read_artifact_number() has a `.next_artifact_number // 1` jq default that masks its own next line's `[ "$next_num" = "null" ]` fallback guard -- the guard can never fire for a genuinely absent field because the default already turned it into the string "1" before the guard runs. Removing the `// 1` default (letting jq emit literal "null" for an absent key) is the fix, not rewriting the guard.

skills/skill-reviser/SKILL.md's Stage 3a already implements a max-prefix (not count) artifact-round reconciliation: after reading next_artifact_number, it separately does `find specs/{NNN}_{slug} -name "[0-9][0-9]_*.md" | sed ... | sort -n | tail -1` across the WHOLE task directory (all artifact-type subdirs together), strips leading zeros with `10#`, and bumps the candidate artifact_number up to max_on_disk+1 whenever it is <= that max. This is the reference pattern to reuse/extract for any other artifact-numbering fix in this codebase rather than re-deriving max-prefix logic from scratch.

In agent-system/extensions/core, no automated task-creation path (commands/task.md Step 6, conclusion-stage.md Step 4c, literature-create-setup-task.sh) ever writes a non-empty artifacts[] at task-creation time -- all either omit the field or write it empty. A defect requiring 'task created with pre-supplied artifacts' as its trigger condition is therefore not reproducible via any current automated core creation path; it implies manual state.json authorship or an external path. Useful when evaluating whether a creation-time fix has a real call site before building one.
